“Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity rose at a solid rate.” Interpreted through New Keynesian policy frameworks and estimated policy rules (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor-rule analyses), this language is clearly positive on real activity. However, given the statement’s concurrent emphasis on below-2% inflation and “patient” guidance, the tone is tempered in a manner consistent with inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford, 2005). The implementation details—maintaining the funds rate range via interest on reserves (Goodfriend, 2002)—reinforce a neutral-to-slightly accommodative stance rather than an overtly hawkish one. Overall: mildly positive but cautious.
